context.description: Canberra is Australia's planned capital, laid out around Lake Burley Griffin by Walter Burley Griffin. Parliament House, the High Court and the national museums, galleries, library and archives stand in a short run along the lake and Anzac Parade, and most are free to enter. Bush-covered hills such as Mount Ainslie, Black Mountain and Red Hill rise within the city, and Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve and the Murrumbidgee River are a short drive south and west.

context.description: Namadgi covers about 46% of the Australian Capital Territory, a mountain landscape of granite tors, waterfalls and snow-capped ranges south-west of Canberra. Walks lead to granite outcrops, 19th-century settlers' huts and Aboriginal rock art, and the Honeysuckle Creek site recalls the Apollo moon landing broadcasts. The visitor centre is on Naas Road near Tharwa village, the park's gateway.
